summary.headline: Neuland Q4 FY26 revenue rose 134.9% YoY to INR788.7 crore and FY26 PAT reached INR363.1 crore, with management flagging lumpiness and weaker Q3.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR788.7 crore, up 134.9% YoY, led by CMS (commercial manufacturing) projects, which contributed over two-thirds of revenue. Gross margin was 62.1% and EBITDA INR319.4 crore (40.5% margin), which management said should not be read as a run-rate. FY26 revenue grew 37.1% to INR2,053.1 crore, EBITDA rose to INR603.4 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT to INR363.1 crore, but free cash flow was negative INR49.4 crore as working capital days rose to 137. Management said FX tailwinds helped and that the business remains lumpy, with Q3 FY26 muted.

segments.name: CMS (commercial manufacturing services)
segments.commentary: Drove Q4 growth and contributed over two-thirds of Q4 revenue. Growth came from volume ramp-up of previously commercialized products plus one new commercialization in FY26; management expects one commercialization in FY27 and one or two later.

segments.name: GDS (development services)
segments.commentary: Softer in FY26 per management. Substantial resources deployed across development, customer engagement and capability building for growth in the short, medium and long term.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Large-scale peptide commercial facility due to be ready by July 2026 as scheduled; 8-10 peptide programs in development, mostly early-stage, with no near- or mid-term revenue expected from the publicly announced early-stage program.

guidance_outlook: No formal quantitative guidance to be given going forward, but management cited 18-20% CAGR as an aspirational, non-linear potential over about 5 years.
FY26 was expected to be a strong year versus FY24; management said Q4 and FY26 performance met expectations, slightly better helped by favourable exchange rates.
Working capital days of 137 expected to normalize in FY27.
Peptide facility ready by July 2026; commercial volumes depend on validation and qualification, with no firm contracts yet.
ROCE expected to moderate as the company enters longer capital deployment cycles.
Growth over the next 2-3 years expected to remain lumpy; management asked investors to judge on a 10-12 quarter trend line.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilization: three units at about 85-90%, the last unit at about 65%.
Large-scale peptide commercial facility being built, targeting peptide fragments and peptide APIs; ready by July 2026.
New R&D centre planned to support complex programs across development stages.
Capital allocation shifting from tactical to long-term; management expects to add INR500 crore a year, possibly INR1,000 crore a year in future, requiring production blocks ahead of demand.
Capex cash outflow FY26 INR397.1 crore.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth aided by shipments made as the rupee depreciated; management put the currency benefit at roughly 10-12% by analyst estimate, which management did not dispute.
Management said volatility comes from shipment timing and newer high-value molecules, and does not expect a return to a steady quarterly run-rate soon.
Funding decline in early-stage biotech discovery has not yet hit the business, which focuses on IND-filed molecules entering Phase I onwards; funnel effect expected over time.
Peptide CDMO market estimated by outside consultants at USD 5-6 billion, supported by GLP-1 and next-generation peptide pipelines.
Freight costs rose late in Q4 due to the Middle East conflict; raw material coverage and price volatility being tracked.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the CDMO growth beyond currency, and were there any order bunching effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth came from existing pipeline, recently commercialized molecules and volume ramp-up, with one new commercialization in FY26. Some volatility is shipment-based and may even out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the early-stage peptide contract a near-term revenue driver?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it is very early-stage with no near- or mid-term revenue expected; it will take at least a few years for commercial benefit. Neuland has 8-10 peptide programs in development.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Esperion (bempedoic acid) change of ownership on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers due to confidentiality. It said supply agreements typically carry inherited clauses, change of ownership does not automatically disrupt supply, and it would flag any short-term issues if seen.

qa_highlights.question: Should investors rely on the 18-20% CAGR and how should margins be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 18-20% a fair but non-linear assumption and aspirational over five years. It said budgets are conservative, so margins tend to beat expectations, and it declined to give H1 vs H2 margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capital allocation becoming longer-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at around INR2,000 crore revenue, the company will add hundreds of crore a year in capex, so it must build production blocks ahead of demand to engage new clients including big pharma.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CEO and MD role change from Sucheth to Saharsh effective April 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a pre-planned role separation: Saharsh focuses on day-to-day operations given his end-to-end CDMO build role, and Sucheth moves to a longer-term role covering the Neuland Foundation, enterprise risk and sustainability.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness and quarter-to-quarter volatility from newer high-value molecules; Q3 FY26 was muted and Q4 was record.
Working capital: days rose to 137 and free cash flow was negative INR49.4 crore in FY26; watch normalization in FY27.
ROCE expected to moderate as larger capital cycles begin; execution risk on capex and peptide facility ramp.
Customer concentration and M&A at sponsor companies (bempedoic acid customer question left unanswered in detail).
FX tailwind inflated Q4 and FY26; freight, raw material and Middle East supply risks.
Unresolved shareholder query on Q3 FY26 transcript wording about inventory, with management promising to revert.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term peptide and CDMO story but deliberately cautious on near-term numbers, repeatedly stressing lumpiness, FX help and non-linear growth. Evasive on specific customers, the 18-20% CAGR framing, H1 vs H2 margins and the Q3 transcript query.
key_quotes: The lumpiness does not recognize financial year boundaries, right?

I would not see us going to a 25% times 4 kind of a situation anytime in the near future, because the moment these newer molecules stabilize, then there's a possibility that some new molecules will come and they will bring in the volatility.
I think the 18% to 20% is a fair assumption not necessarily linearly.
I think it has the potential to create another Neuland for sure.
